{{Top|leg}}
The '''stateless strategy''' was a [[Space warfare/Legends|space warfare]] strategy utilized throughout [[The galaxy/Legends|galactic history]]. Properly used, it allowed a smaller power to defeat a larger, militarily-superior one.<ref name="Atlas">''[[The Essential Atlas]]''</ref>

==The strategy==
{{Quote|Control space and you control any battlefield you can imagine. Unfortunately you cannot control space.|[[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Firmus Nantz]]|<ref name="Warfare">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref>}}
The stateless strategy relied on decentralization and the sheer vastness of space to allow a smaller belligerent to beat a larger one. A power with a defined [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld]] and colonies could be reduced and defeated with numerical superiority. However, a decentralized power without a clearly-defined homeworld or territory would have to be overcome everywhere it existed before it could be defeated. The vastness of space meant that throughout history, even the largest militaries found controlling space impossible.<ref name="Atlas" />

In contrast, this gave an advantage to the decentralized belligerent: since the larger opponent could not defend everywhere, the smaller power could choose its battles and strike where its opponent was not. This would force the larger power into making the choice between heavily-defending a handful of key "[[Fortress world/Legends|fortress worlds]]," thus allowing the enemy a free hand elsewhere, or dispersing their forces and so risking the loss of a key [[Planet/Legends|planet]] through defeat in detail. [[Galactic economy|Economic]] considerations and public pressure tended to force states to adopt the fortress world strategy.<ref name="Atlas" />

==History==
The various [[Sith Empire/Legends|Sith Empires]] throughout history used the stateless strategy in their wars against the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]].<ref name="Atlas" /> The [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] used the strategy during the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. However, since they possessed territory, the CIS was vulnerable to the stateless strategy in its own right, and by [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]] had been forced on to the defensive in the [[Outer Rim Sieges/Legends|Outer Rim Sieges]] once the Republic's superior industrial base had produced enough [[Warship/Legends|warships]] to both defend their territories and take the offensive.<ref name="Warfare" />

The [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Alliance to Restore the Republic]] made use of the stateless strategy during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. The [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] response was a policy of reprisal, a system of state terror that was institutionalized in the [[Tarkin Doctrine/Legends|Tarkin Doctrine]].<ref name="Imperial Sourcebook">''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]''</ref> However, the policy of overwhelming force in an effort to deny the Rebels safe haven did more to foment resistance than eliminate it. The creation of the [[Death Star/Legends|Death Star]] was intended to reverse such a state of affairs by introducing the possibility of a reprisal so terrifying - namely, the destruction of entire planets - that no world would risk aiding the Rebellion. In the aftermath of the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the Empire retreated to the "fortress world" strategy, effectively giving the Rebellion a free hand over much of the galaxy and dooming it as a galactic power.<ref name="Atlas" />

[[Grand Admiral/Legends|Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo/Legends|Thrawn's]] [[Thrawn campaign|final campaign]] against the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] in [[9 ABY/Legends|9 ABY]] was considered to be a classic example of the stateless strategy. Making use of high-profile raids against poorly-defended targets, Thrawn panicked the New Republic's citizens and made it look weak when it could not defend all its worlds. Thrawn made a series of feints at [[Ando/Legends|Ando]], [[Filve]] and [[Crondre/Legends|Crondre]] that forced the New Republic fleet at [[Ord Pardron/Legends|Ord Pardron]] to a sortie. Thrawn then [[Battle of Ord Pardron|destroyed]] the undefended [[Ord Pardron sector defense outpost|military base]] at Ord Pardron, in turn allowing him to [[Battle at Ukio|capture Ukio]]. The campaign totally reversed the strategic geography of the Galactic Civil War, forcing the New Republic to adopt the fortress world strategy, with rapid reaction fleets deployed to defend [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]], [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]] and [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]], until it was abruptly ended with Thrawn's assassination at the [[Battle of Bilbringi (9 ABY)|Battle of Bilbringi]].<ref name="Warfare" />
